evidence.description: Every enabled invocation of initialize() calls initBraze without checking whether initialization has already occurred.
Initialization replaces the stored SDK instance, while a deferred task configures the presenter through the mutable braze property.

candidates.explanation: Repeated initialization replaces the SDK instance and launches additional asynchronous setup. Because presenter setup accesses the current braze property rather than the instance created by that invocation, a task from an earlier initialization can configure a later instance. Initialization therefore has overlapping, order-dependent effects.
candidates.title: Repeated initialization can overlap SDK setup

evidence.description: The helper obtains the application's shared notification center and sets its entire category collection to the Braze categories.

candidates.explanation: setNotificationCategories replaces the notification center's registered category set; it does not add categories to it. Calling this helper therefore removes any previously registered categories outside the Braze collection, potentially disabling their notification actions. This is an application-wide side effect of obtaining the notification center.
candidates.title: Notification setup replaces all registered categories

evidence.description: The sole CustomEvent case has an empty raw value.
The event raw value is passed directly to the SDK as the event name.

candidates.explanation: Every event expressible through this public API is logged with an empty name. Consequently, the API cannot represent a meaningful named custom event and passes an invalid event name to Braze.
candidates.title: Custom-event API only produces an empty event name

evidence.description: The authorization-status refresh occurs only after a throwing authorization request completes successfully.
The refresh path discards errors from that request.

candidates.explanation: If requestAuthorization throws, execution exits before notificationAuthorizationStatus is refreshed, despite the stated guarantee that it is always updated. The refresh caller also suppresses that error, leaving a failed authorization operation indistinguishable from a completed refresh and potentially leaving the cached status outdated.
candidates.title: Authorization errors skip the status refresh
